scope: src/main.js lines 6049-9200 (Enemy class state machine + tactical AI) plus the AI methods that span beyond the boundary: tactical helpers (10807-11133), the core update()/state-machine switch (11134-11859), _updateAnim pose selection (8295-8398), takeDamage (7872-8108), canSee (10319-10381), EnemyManager.update awareness/suppress (12814-12940), _bakeCoverSlots (12119-12165).

findings.title: SUPPRESS / HOLD_CORNER / PEEK_FIRE state enums are declared but never assigned to this.state
findings.description: The tactical FSM constants HOLD_CORNER=6, PEEK_FIRE=7, SUPPRESS=9 are defined and documented as states layered on ATTACK, but a repo-wide grep for `state\s*=\s*(SUPPRESS|HOLD_CORNER|PEEK_FIRE)` returns ZERO assignments. The suppress mechanic actually runs via the per-enemy flags this.suppressUntil / this.suppressBurstsLeft (set in EnemyManager._tryFormPairs line 12709-12710 and Squad.update line 12330-12331) while the enemy stays in ATTACK. Consequently every branch keyed on `this.state===SUPPRESS` is unreachable: the suppress POSE at line 8383 (`else if(this.state===SUPPRESS)poseState='suppress';`) never fires, the SUPPRESS locomotion 'run' mapping at line 6148 never fires, and the awareness-propagation guard `a.state===PEEK_FIRE` at line 12866 is always false (redundant with the ATTACK check beside it).
findings.evidence:
const PATROL=0,...,HOLD_CORNER=6,PEEK_FIRE=7,REPOSITION=8,SUPPRESS=9;  // line 6063
... else if(this.state===SUPPRESS)poseState='suppress';  // line 8383 — state never equals SUPPRESS
... if(!(a.state===CHASE||a.state===ATTACK||a.state===PEEK_FIRE))continue;  // line 12866 — PEEK_FIRE never assigned
findings.fix: Decide one of two paths. (A) If suppress is meant to be a real visible pose: in the ATTACK case where _isSuppressing is computed (line 11811) set this.state=SUPPRESS while suppressing and restore to ATTACK when suppressBurstsLeft hits 0, so the dedicated 'suppress' pose at 8383 and the run locomotion at 6148 actually drive. (B) If suppress is intentionally a flag-only overlay, delete the dead `this.state===SUPPRESS` pose branch (8383), the SUPPRESS term in the locomotion map (6148), and the `a.state===PEEK_FIRE` term (12866) to remove the contradiction. Path A gives a visible AAA win (distinct hunkered suppress stance); path B is the zero-risk cleanup.
findings.risk: Path A changes which animation pose plays for suppressing enemies — verify the 'suppress' pose exists in ENEMY_POSE_STATES and reads well; keep the existing flag-based fire-gating untouched so suppression fire behavior is unchanged. Path B is cosmetic dead-code removal, no behavioral change. Either keeps build/probes green.

findings.title: Hard 22m vision cap in canSee() defeats sniper/marksman attackRange (up to ~27m)
findings.description: canSee() returns false for any target beyond 22m for ALL enemy types (single hardcoded `if(dist>22)return false`). But sniper attackRange is `22+diff*1.2` (≈26.8m at diff 4) and marksman is `20+diff*1.0` (≈24m). The CHASE→ATTACK transition at line 11462 requires `horizDist<=this.attackRange && cs`; since cs is forced false past 22m, a sniper/marksman can never engage at the upper half of its own stated range. It is dragged inward (CHASE at 11457 with no LOS sends it to SEARCH/closer) until within 22m, so the 'long sightline' fantasy and the LONG SIGHTLINE toast (line 11472) are undercut. The archetype's defining trait (reach) is silently clamped.
findings.evidence:
const dist=Math.sqrt(dx*dx+dz*dz);if(dist>22)return false;  // line 10327
// vs TS sniper rng:22+diff*1.2, marksman rng:20+diff*1.0 (lines 6298,6307)
findings.fix: Make the vision cap per-archetype. Replace the constant 22 with a per-enemy sight distance, e.g. `const _sight=this.attackRange+ (this.type==='sniper'||this.type==='marksman'?6:2); if(dist>Math.max(22,_sight))return false;` so snipers/marksmen see across their full engagement band while others keep ~22m. Keep the existing smoke/wall sampling unchanged.
findings.risk: Slightly longer canSee raycasts for snipers (more sample steps at long range) but only for 1-2 archetypes; the spatial wall index already bounds cost. Could make snipers engage from farther — that is the intended buff. Re-run the 32 static probes; no save-compat impact.

findings.title: Riot charge and shielded body-block move the enemy, then the ATTACK switch-case moves it AGAIN the same frame
findings.description: The archetype pre-state hooks (lines 11337-11407) run BEFORE the `switch(this.state)` at 11422 and there is no break/return between them. For a riot in ATTACK within 6m, line 11341 issues a sprint rush via _moveWithVelocity; the code then falls through into `case ATTACK` which runs the default circular-strafe _moveWithVelocity at 11673 (and _maybeReposition/juke). Two competing velocity integrations per frame: the strafe overwrites/dilutes the committed melee rush, so the riot wobbles sideways instead of bull-rushing. Same double-move for shielded (body-block move at 11376 then ATTACK strafe). The drone swarm hook at 11404 has the same shape but drone has its own early-return ATTACK fire path so it is less affected.
findings.fix: When the riot melee-charge (or shielded body-block) hook actually drives movement, set a flag and have the ATTACK case skip its strafe/juke movement block for that enemy this frame — e.g. set `this._archetypeMovedThisFrame=true` in the hook and guard the ATTACK 'else' strafe branch (line 11658-11677) with `&& !this._archetypeMovedThisFrame`. Reset the flag at top of update(). Keeps shooting logic intact; only suppresses the conflicting second move.
findings.risk: Riot will commit harder to the charge (intended, more threatening). Verify riot still fires while charging (the ATTACK fire block after the move stays reachable). Low risk to other archetypes since the guard only trips when a hook moved the enemy.

findings.title: Demolitions cover-aware grenade target uses best.peekDx/peekDz without the ||0 guard used elsewhere
findings.description: Line 11419 builds `_demolitionsTarget` as `new THREE.Vector3(best.x+best.peekDx*1.2,0,best.z+best.peekDz*1.2)`. The same coverSlots array is read defensively at line 10839 as `s.peekDx||0`. Baked slots (_bakeCoverSlots) always define peekDx/peekDz, but if any authored level-data coverSlot lacks them, `best.peekDx` is undefined → `x + undefined*1.2` = NaN. That NaN target is then passed into spawnEnemyGrenade at line 11699, throwing the grenade to NaN world coords (vanishes / lands at an undefined spot). Inconsistent with the guarded sibling read.
findings.risk: Pure hardening; identical behavior for baked slots which always have peekDx. No save-compat or perf concern.

findings.title: Enemy gunfire casts NO dynamic light — flat additive sprite only; player gun has a PointLight muzzle flash
findings.description: Enemy muzzleLight is hardcoded null (line 7049) 'for perf', so enemy muzzle flashes are pure additive plane sprites that never illuminate the surrounding geometry. The player's own weapon DOES get a PointLight muzzle flash (line 16811). In a dark room-clearing shooter, an enemy firing from a shadowed corner should briefly strobe light onto nearby walls/floor — this is one of the highest-impact 'looks AAA instantly' cues and its absence reads as flat. A single pooled, budgeted light shared across all enemies (lit only at the nearest firing enemy for one frame) avoids the original per-enemy-light perf cliff.
findings.fix: Add ONE shared scene PointLight (e.g. G._enemyMuzzleLight, intensity 0, distance ~5, color 0xffcc66) created once. In EnemyManager.update, when a shot fires, position it at `mp` (getMuzzlePos), set intensity ~3.2*_flashMul, and decay it to 0 over ~60ms in the frame loop (or via the same setTimeout that hides the sprites at line 12919). This bounds dynamic lights to exactly one regardless of enemy count, sidestepping the shader-hitch reason the per-enemy light was removed.
findings.risk: One extra PointLight in the lighting budget — verify it does not push past the renderer's max-lights and trigger a shader recompile; keep intensity/decay short. Tone-mapping/exposure unchanged. Keeps probes green (no API surface change).

findings.title: Being shot while on PATROL jumps straight to CHASE without setting lastKnownPos, so CHASE can immediately bounce back to PATROL
findings.description: takeDamage line 8102 does `if(this.state===PATROL)this.state=CHASE;` but never sets this.lastKnownPos. In the CHASE case (line 11457) if the enemy has no LOS and horizDist>14, it falls into `if(this.lastKnownPos){SEARCH}else{PATROL}` — with lastKnownPos still null it drops straight back to PATROL, so an enemy shot from beyond 14m and out of sight can flip CHASE→PATROL the very next frame, looking like it 'forgot' it was just shot. The ALERT path (line 11427) correctly sets lastKnownPos; this damage-triggered path skips it.
findings.fix: On the damage-triggered wake, seed a last-known position toward the shooter so CHASE has something to pursue: in takeDamage, when waking from PATROL, set `this.lastKnownPos=this.group.position.clone().addScaledVector(this.staggerDir,-4);` (staggerDir points away from attacker, so -4 along it heads toward the shot's origin) and bump alertFlashTimer. Or route through ALERT (this.state=ALERT;this.alertTimer=.2) so the existing ALERT logic runs.
findings.risk: Makes shot-while-patrolling enemies investigate instead of dozing off — improves reactivity. Low risk; staggerDir is already normalized at line 7906. No save-compat impact.

findings.title: Visor base-color cache constructs a Color from visorM.color then immediately .copy() overwrites it
findings.description: Line 10110 lazily caches `this._visorBaseCol = new THREE.Color(this.visorM.color).copy(this.visorGlowM.color)`. The `new THREE.Color(this.visorM.color)` constructor argument is pointless because `.copy(this.visorGlowM.color)` overwrites every channel on the next call in the same expression. The cached base ends up being the visorGlow color, not a blend — confusing and a wasted constructor read. Cosmetically the visor still pulses correctly so there is no visible bug, just dead/misleading code computed once per enemy.
findings.fix: Drop the no-op argument: `this._visorBaseCol=new THREE.Color().copy(this.visorGlowM.color)` (or `this.visorGlowM.color.clone()`). If the intent was actually to blend visor + glow hues, do it explicitly with .lerp; otherwise the clone is the honest form.
findings.risk: Zero behavioral change (cached value is identical); trivial. No perf or save concern.

findings.title: _markShotVisual recoil side has an 18% random sign-flip that can kick recoil toward the peek-out side
findings.description: Line 10912 computes the shot recover side as `(this.peekAmt>.10?(this._peekSideSign||1):(this.strafeDir||1))*(Math.random()<.18?-1:1)`. When peeking, _peekSideSign encodes which way the body leaned out of cover; the trailing random `*-1` (18% chance) flips the recoil/recover lean to the WRONG side ~1 shot in 6, momentarily reading as the enemy recoiling back INTO cover the wrong direction. It is subtle but inconsistent with the deliberate peek-side bias the rest of the system maintains.
findings.fix: Only apply the random flip when NOT actively peeking, where there is no committed side: `const base=this.peekAmt>.10?(this._peekSideSign||1):(this.strafeDir||1)*(Math.random()<.18?-1:1);` i.e. move the random term inside the strafe branch so a peek shot always recoils consistent with the peek side.
findings.risk: Very low — purely a recoil-pose polish tweak; does not affect aim/damage. Keeps probes green.
